### StatusBarChipProps

```ts
type StatusBarChipProps = Omit<
  ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>,
  "children"
> &
  object;
```

Props accepted by StatusBarChip.

#### Type Declaration

| Name        | Type        | Description                                                                                                           |
| ----------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`     | `ReactNode` | Visible name of the item, e.g. "Ports".                                                                               |
| `icon?`     | `ReactNode` | Decorative mark before the label; on a phone the chip shows it alone.                                                 |
| `readout?`  | `ReactNode` | A readout after the label, such as a CountBadge.                                                                      |
| `pressed?`  | `boolean`   | Toggle state. `undefined` is an ordinary action; a boolean adds `aria-pressed` and fills the chip while on.           |
| `expanded?` | `boolean`   | Disclosure state for a chip that opens a menu or panel. A boolean adds `aria-expanded` and fills the chip while open. |

## Variables

### StatusBarChip

```ts
const StatusBarChip: ForwardRefExoticComponent<
  Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "children"> &
    object &
    RefAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>
>;
```

One App-declared status bar control (an action, a toggle or a menu trigger): a
flat chip with the same quiet face as StatusBarPicker. It forwards its ref and
props, so a menu can render it as its trigger.

One App window's status bar: its attachment first, then the App's own readouts,

### StatusBarPicker()
